quote: AP was previously owned by Insight Partners, a venture capital and private equity firm.
status_event: Acquired by Vistria Group in 2019; now trades as Risepoint.
notes: No source on the terms of the November 2011 entry could be read, so the question is not settled. The Wikipedia sentence cites only the firm's own portfolio page and is not a sale article naming the firm as seller. The FTC notice of 2019-11-26 (https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/early-termination-notices/20200231) lists "Acquired Party Academic Partnerships, LLC" and no Insight fund; that is weak either way because the firm invests through several parallel funds. The Forbes article of 2014-02-12 that Wikipedia cites returned HTTP 403; the Internet Archive was on the machine-wide cooldown and was not touched. Entry date is the panel date.

quote: received a majority investment from Insight Partners and subsequently joined forces with i2i Population Health
status_event: Insight Partners took a majority investment and merged it with i2i Population Health in 2025.
notes: The cited release is from Aeris Partners, the financial adviser to Azara and its prior investor Hughes & Company, dated 2025-02-19. The second adviser, Healthcare Growth Partners, titles its notice "HGP Advises Insight Partners in Acquisition of Azara Healthcare" (https://hgp.com/research-news/hgp-advises-insight-partners-in-acquisition-of-azara-healthcare/). The firm's own post only says it "led the merger and invested in the newly combined company"; "Insight joins existing Azara Healthcare investor Hughes & Company." Three of the firm's people joined the board. HQ from the release dateline (Burlington, Mass.); the panel has no location.

quote: The New York venture capital and private equity firm Insight Partners has bought majority ownership of CivicPlus for $290 million.
status_event: Insight Partners bought majority ownership for $290M in 2021; still privately held.
notes: The firm's own post calls it "a $290 million investment" and does not state the stake; GovTech states majority ownership twice and calls the firm "the company's new owners". HQ is Manhattan, Kansas.

quote: has snapped up Conga too, which had been acquired by private equity investor Insight Venture Partners in April 2015
status_event: Combined with Thoma Bravo-owned Apttus in 2020 in a deal reported at $715M; Insight kept a stake.
sources_checked: Form D AppExtremes Group Holdings, LLC 2019
notes: Second source, the Thoma Bravo release of 2020-05-07: "Nikitas Koutoupes, Managing Director at Insight Partners, the majority stakeholder in Conga, will also join the Board of Managers." (https://www.thomabravo.com/press-releases/apttus-and-conga-combine-to-become-leader-in-digitally-transforming-commercial-operations). The firm's own 2015 post says only "a $70 million investment" into a "boot-strapped" company. Form D of the holding company AppExtremes Group Holdings, LLC (incorporated 2015, first sale 2015-08-10, issuer address in Broomfield, so not an acquisition vehicle under the address test) lists three of the firm's people as directors beside the CEO. Dates differ by source: panel and diginomica say April 2015, the release is dated 2015-06-25. The $715M figure is below $1B.

status_event: No exit found; ELK Holdco, LLC filed Form D notices each year from 2022 to 2025.
sources_checked: PR Newswire continuation fund release 2023 (no mention)
notes: The quote is the issuer street address field of the Form D signed 2022-07-22 for ELK Holdco, LLC (Delaware LLC, year of incorporation 2021, first sale 2022-04-07, securities are profits interest units). Related persons at "Insight Partners", "1114 Avenue of the Americas, 36th floor": Deven Parekh ("Member of the Board of Managers"), Anika Agarwal ("Member of the Board of Managers and Vice President"), Byron Lictenstein ("Member of the Board of Managers"), Andrew Prodromos ("Vice President"). That is three of the five board managers; the other two (Kamal Patel, Ajay Kapare) sit at 200 Riverfront Blvd, Elmwood Park. No press release on the deal was found, so no round word. Entry date is inferred from the vehicle's year of incorporation; the panel gives none.

quote: Insight had a 55 per cent stake in Fenergo, having invested $75 million in the fintech in 2015.
status_event: Acquired by Astorg and Bridgepoint in 2021 at a reported valuation above $1B.
notes: The 55 per cent figure is the stake at the 2021 sale, after later holders (DXC, ABN AMRO, BNP Paribas) came in, so the entry stake was at least a majority if the firm bought nothing more in between; no entry-time article stating majority could be read (AltAssets is paywalled). Sources differ on who put in the $75M: The Deal says "New York-based Insight Partners and Aquiline Capital Partners LLC invested $75 million in Fenergo in 2015." and that Aquiline left in 2018 (https://www.thedeal.com/private-equity/insight-partners-exits-fenergo/). Round word is from the panel milestone ("led Fenergo's $75M private equity round"). Announced 2015-07-15, panel date August 2015. Priced valuation of $1B or more: "Industry sources estimate that the deal values Fenergo at $1.165 billion", Irish Times, 2021-04-30, same URL.

quote: La participation de ce nouveau partenaire reste minoritaire
status_event: Insight took a minority stake in 2021 for more than EUR 300M; still privately held.
sources_checked: Les Echos and Capital Finance 2021-02-19 (403, not read)
notes: CONTRADICTS the judge's note (a majority stake bought from IK). The quote is the chief executive, Clement Delpirou, speaking to ImmoMatin on 2021-02-22; the same passage says it is neither a sale nor a taking of control. Second source, counsel to the co-founders (Hoche Avocats, 2021-04-29): "L’investisseur américain prend une participation minoritaire pour plus de 300 M€, valorisant IAD environ 1,2 milliard d’euros" (https://www.hoche-avocats.com/hoche-avocats-conseille-les-co-fondateurs-diad-dans-le-cadre-dune-levee-record-aupres-du-vc-americain-insight-partners/). What may explain the judge's reading: IK lists its 2016 fund position as realised in April 2021 and says "IK Partners reinvested in iad alongside Insight Partners, Five Arrows Principal Investments and Naxicap Partners in April 2021." (https://ikpartners.com/investments/iad-2/), so the existing holders rolled over while the firm came in. Whether that consortium counts as a group purchase of control is a ruling for the judge; the firm's own stake is stated as minority. Priced valuation of $1B or more: about EUR 1.2B, Hoche Avocats, 2021-04-29. Announced 2021-02-19, closed April 2021; the firm's post calls it a "strategic investment".

quote: District-based Interfolio, which makes software for college and university faculty members, is set to be acquired by Insight Venture Partners.
status_event: Acquired by Elsevier (RELX) from Insight Partners in 2022.
notes: The article is the Washington Business Journal's, carried by WTOP; it reports a price of more than $110M from a source and notes the chief executive called the deal an investment. Second source, the firm's own counsel (Willkie, 2022-06-09): "Willkie previously advised Insight Partners in its acquisition of Interfolio in 2018." (https://www.willkie.com/news/2022/06/elsevier-acquires-interfolio-from-insight-partners); the same notice is titled "Elsevier Acquires Interfolio from Insight Partners". An earlier round on record (January 2016, $12M Series A) was not the firm's. Announced 2018-11-26, panel date December 2018.

quote: Mediware is purchasing Kinnser from Insight Venture Partners.
status_event: Acquired by Mediware Information Systems, a TPG Capital company, in 2017.
notes: SOURCES PULL TWO WAYS. The sale release names the firm as the seller, which is the sale-as-owner signal. But the firm's own entry post uses a venture round word: "Kinnser Software announced today that it has secured Series A financing from Insight Venture Partners" (https://www.insightpartners.com/ideas/kinnser-software-announces-investment-from-insight-venture-partners/), $40M, two board seats. No source states majority or minority for 2012. Confidence is set to low rather than medium for that reason. The 2012 Form D is filed by the company itself at its Austin address ($39,900,000 sold, 7 investors), so it is not an acquisition vehicle. In the sale release the chief executive thanks "Insight Venture Partners and Georgian Partners", so a second investor held shares by 2017.

quote: today announced the closing of a $35.8 million minority equity investment from Insight Venture Partners
status_event: No exit found; the company website was live on 2026-09-26.
notes: The release on the firm's site states minority in its first sentence. The 2015 Form D is a different question from the entry: issuer Mediaspectrum, Inc., incorporated 2015, 1111 Lincoln Road, Miami Beach, total offering $12, with two of the firm's people as directors beside four others; it may record a later reorganisation and does not change the entry. HQ is the panel's (Miami Beach); the 2013 release describes "a Boston-based company".

quote: In March, PayIt made headlines with a more than $100 million investment by New York-based Insight Partners, which provided an exit for investors within the KCRise Fund
status_event: Raised a further $90M from Macquarie Capital in 2022; still privately held.
notes: No source read states majority or minority. Signals that lean to control, none of them decisive: the round bought out earlier holders (quote above); TechCrunch says "The funding is coming from a single investor, Insight Partners" and that the company had raised only $11M before; the Form D issuer PayIt Holdings, LLC was incorporated in 2019 and lists the firm's Blair Flicker as Secretary and Ryan Hinkle and Rebecca Liu-Doyle as directors, all c/o Insight Partners, 1114 6th Avenue. Signals against: the issuer address is the company's own (1812 Broadway Blvd, Kansas City), so it fails the address test for an acquisition vehicle; the firm holds two of four board seats named on the filing; Weatherford Capital stayed in and added $25M in May 2019; Silicon Prairie News calls it a "round ... led by" the firm.

quote: Thoma Bravo is buying Planview from Insight Venture Partners, a New York-based venture capital firm that acquired the company in 2013.
status_event: Sold to Thoma Bravo in 2017 with Insight keeping a minority, then to TPG Capital and TA Associates in 2020 for $1.6B.
notes: Second source, the buyer's release: "Thoma Bravo will become the new majority shareholder of Planview upon the closing of the transaction, while Insight Venture Partners will maintain its original 2014 capital investment in the company." (https://www.thomabravo.com/press-releases/thoma-bravo-to-acquire-planview); its opening line says Thoma Bravo agreed "to acquire Planview from Insight Venture Partners". The firm's own 2013 post is vaguer: "Insight Venture Partners has acquired a substantial interest in the company", with a new chief executive named and three board seats. Small date mismatch: the Thoma Bravo release says 2014, the firm and the panel say December 2013. Priced valuation of $1B or more: $1.6B, sale to TPG Capital and TA Associates, Austin American-Statesman headline of 2020-12-18 (https://www.statesman.com/story/business/2020/12/18/private-equity-firms-close-1-6-billion-deal-austin-based-planview/3961608001/, headline only, body not read).

quote: Carbon Relay and Insight Partners today announced a $63 million transaction to accelerate the growth of its Red Sky Ops solution
status_event: Acquired by CloudBolt Software, another Insight company, in 2025.
notes: No source read states majority or minority. The release avoids a round word and says "transaction"; the press rewrote it as a round: "announced Tuesday that it closed on a $63 million funding round led by Insight Partners" (https://www.builtinboston.com/articles/carbon-relay-raises-63m). The 2025 sale does not help: the buyer is itself held by the firm ("TNS owner Insight Partners is an investor in: StormForge, CloudBolt Software.", The New Stack), and no article names the firm as seller or owner. No Form D was found for the company or a vehicle.

quote: Another significant transaction in the public safety training, compliance and workforce management sector was the acquisition of Vector Solutions by Genstar and Insight Partners.
status_event: Genstar Capital and Insight Partners bought it from Golden Gate Capital in 2021; still privately held.
notes: Control here is a group purchase: the firm is named as a co-acquirer, its own share is not stated and is likely the smaller one. The deal release names only Genstar as the majority buyer and does not mention the firm: Genstar "announced today an agreement to acquire a majority ownership stake in Vector Solutions" and "Genstar is acquiring Vector from Golden Gate Capital, a leading private equity investment firm, which will remain a significant shareholder in the business." (https://www.vectorsolutions.com/resources/press-releases/genstar-capital-to-acquire-majority-stake-in-vector-solutions/). The GovTech piece is a guest roundup by a banker (Jeff Cook), one sentence, so medium. Announced 2021-05-14, panel date July 2021 (the close).

quote: on its sale to VisualLogix, Inc., a portfolio company of Insight Partners
status_event: Bought M.E.P.CAD and, in 2026, refyne Group; still privately held.
sources_checked: Peak Technology Partners notice (Mar 17, year not shown)
notes: No source states majority, minority or how the firm came in; the verdict rests on the pattern and is low for that reason. What the sources show: the company is a group assembled from purchases (AutoSPRINK and AlarmCAD from M.E.P.CAD, Metal Building Software, refyne Group), its chief executive says these are the products "around which we are building VisualLogix", the only investor any source names is the firm, and no funding round is on record. The cited notice is from the seller's adviser in the M.E.P.CAD sale. The company's own releases do not mention the firm at all. Entry date unknown: the panel has none and the earliest dated item on the company site is December 8, 2025. HQ is taken from the release dateline (NEW YORK); the panel has no location.
